title: Inis chrom's lofts rebuilt on piles
summary: After the storm tide drowns its net-lofts and rope-walk, Inis chrom does not ask An Crùn for its rebuilding. Its own carpenters raise both a second time on driven piles a fathom above the old floor, timber floated down the Abhainn ghorm from the woods above Àth gharbh, the work finished before the autumn herring.

title: Cnoc leathan's sixth parish school
summary: The last and smallest of Cnoc leathan's six new parish schools opens with eleven children on its benches and a teacher hired from Baile chiar. The council's clerk, sent to ask how the shire paid for six schools at once, is shown plain accounts and asks nothing further.

title: Catrìona nic Neacail lent to the search
summary: Comhairle nam Mèinnean names eleven surveyors to Alasdair mac Ùisdein's Sireadh na Dàrna Fèithe. Catrìona nic Neacail, thirty-two, a chain-hand risen through the vein-towns, is one of them, and tells a senior surveyor riding out with her that she would rather walk ground and find nothing than be told years on that nobody looked.

title: The first shaft above Dùn dhearg
summary: The search's first shaft goes down above Dùn dhearg in stone that gives every hopeful sign, the diggers wagering small coin among themselves on the day the vein will show. It is judged barren within the fortnight, the first entry in a tally that will run to forty-one.

title: The moor's own name, am Fearann Falamh
summary: An old digger of Dùn dhearg tells Catrìona nic Neacail the moor's shepherds have long called the search's ground am Fearann Falamh, meaning only that no shepherd ever found a spring there worth the digging. The name outlasts the search's own hope of it.

title: The forty-first shaft struck dry
summary: The last shaft of the search, sunk on the moor south of Baile ruadh through the hardest weather any of the forty had asked, strikes water at a depth no vein has ever answered. Catrìona nic Neacail writes the word barren in her own field-book a forty-first time and sits a while on the spoil-heap before riding to report it.

title: Mòrag nic Coinnich finds An Aois Naomh roll
summary: Cataloguing an Leabharlann's lower room, Mòrag nic Coinnich finds a Holy Age survey naming the same hills above Dùn dhearg and moors south of Baile ruadh, searched once and found barren ages before, the surveyors' own names worn from the roll. She sends Catrìona nic Neacail word the same week the forty-first shaft is closed.

title: An Leabharlann's copy of the old survey promised south
summary: Catrìona nic Neacail copies Mòrag nic Coinnich's letter into her own field-book beside her last entry and resolves to see An Aois Naomh roll sent south in copy, so that any surveyor sent to the same ground again will not have to wait on a keeper's own cataloguing to learn what the last search cost.

title: Seonaid nic Ghill-Eathain's letter read a second time
summary: A Board clerk sorting the year's correspondence finds Seonaid nic Ghill-Eathain's letter on the search, filed unread when it was first sent, and carries it to Catrìona nic Neacail along with Mòrag nic Coinnich's. Catrìona keeps a copy of both beside her own last entry, though she judges the school's question and the Board's chain answer to different masters.

title: Dùn dhearg's shepherds testify at the circuit court
summary: At the circuit court's hearing of Dùn dhearg's claim, two shepherds swear that grazing spoiled by the search's spoil-heaps is lost longer than any digger reckoned, one saying he lost more lambs to the search's own open ground in two years than to wolves in ten. The court finds for the town.

title: The Mac Ùisdein stone house let to the Board
summary: Its coin thinned by the search and Dùn dhearg's damages, Taigh Mhic Ùisdein lets its stone house at Cathair mhòr, kept in the family since the first holder's day, to Comhairle nam Mèinnean, which moves its offices into it the following spring.

title: The child of Baile ruadh lost to an open shaft
summary: A child of Baile ruadh, out after a stray lamb on ground she has walked without harm a hundred times, falls into one of the search's uncovered shafts and is not found until the day after. The parish's own book holds her name and the day, and nothing more.

title: Baile ruadh votes to fence the forty-one shafts
summary: The shire of Baile ruadh votes to fence every one of the search's forty-one shafts at its own cost rather than wait on An Crùn, and enters a claim against Taigh Mhic Ùisdein for the fencing's cost that is never paid. The fencing goes up through the summer, post and wire round every covered mouth.

title: A mother takes the long road at Baile ruadh
summary: The mother of the child lost in the open shaft at Baile ruadh will not walk that road again the whole of the year after, and takes the longer way round by the mill whatever the weather asks of her.

title: Sheep fall into the open shafts
summary: On the moor south of Baile ruadh, where the ground is softest and the covering poorest, sheep begin falling into the search's open shaft-mouths before the first winter is out, three that the shire's reckoning can put a number to and likely more that no reckoning counts.
